t: Life-Sketch of Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Ji Maharaj (Dakshin)
grp: Life-Sketch of Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Ji Maharaj (Dakshin)

c.b:
The First Acharya of the 20th Century, Supremely Venerable, Ever to Be Remembered at Dawn
| | |
|---|---|
| Birth | Ashadha Krishna 6, V.S. 1929 (1872 CE), a Wednesday. |
| Birthplace and name | Yelgul (Maharashtra); Satgauda Patil (Jain). |
| Parents | Shrimati Satyavati and Bhimgauda Patil. |
| Kshullaka Diksha | Jyeshtha Shukla 13, V.S. 1972 (1915 CE), at Uttur village (Maharashtra). |
| Ailaka Diksha | At Girnar Ji Siddhakshetra, at the feet of Bhagwan Neminath on the fifth tonk (peak). |
| Muni Diksha | Phalguna Shukla 14, V.S. 1976 (1920 CE), at Yarnal village (Karnataka). |
| Diksha-Guru for Kshullaka and Muni Diksha | Muni Shri Devendrakirti Ji Maharaj. |
| Acharya Pada (Acharya-ship) | Ashwina Shukla 11, V.S. 1981 (1924 CE), at Samdoli village, on a Wednesday. On that very day Acharya Shri conferred 2 Muni dikshas, 1 Ailaka diksha and 1 Kshullika diksha. |
| Charitra Chakravarti (title) | V.S. 1994 (1937 CE), on the auspicious occasion of the Panchakalyanak Pratishtha at Gajpantha Siddhakshetra. |
| Auspicious vihar and chaturmas in North India | Marga­shirsha Krishna 1, V.S. 1984 (1927 CE), setting out to pay homage at Tirthraj Sammed Shikhar Ji, at the request of Seth Gendamal Ji of Bombay, the sanghapati. Completed 11 chaturmas in North India from 1928 onward. |
| Pada-vihar (journeys on foot) | Travelled more than 35,000 miles on foot during his life of restraint. |
| Tapa-sadhana (austerities) | While performing many vows such as Simhanishkridita, Charitrashuddhi, Tees Chaubisi and Kavalachandrayana, he completed a total of 9,938 fasts (upavasa) in his lifetime, along with rasa-parityaga (renunciation of tastes) and many other external and internal austerities. |
| Total chaturmas | Completed 41 chaturmas during his initiated life. |
| Initiated disciples | 26 Munis, 4 Aryikas, 16 Ailakas, 28 Kshullakas, 14 Kshullikas, and a fourfold sangha of hundreds of vow-taking (vrati) shravakas. |
| Special | In 1925 he graced with his presence the Mahamastakabhisheka of Gommateshwar Bhagwan Bahubali Swami. From Shravanabelagola onward he came to be called "Gurunam Guru" — the Guru of Gurus. |
| | For the protection of Jain temples he gave up taking grain (anna) for 3 years and 12 days, thereby protecting the Dharma and its culture. |
| | To protect the Shatkhandagama and Mahabandha scriptures — written on palm-leaves — from insects, he had those texts engraved on copper plates. |
| Adoption of Utkrishta Sallekhana | On 24 October 1951 (V.S. 2008) he adopted the twelve-year Utkrishta (supreme) Sallekhana at Gajpantha Siddhakshetra. |
| Conferring his own Acharya Pada | In the midst of his 36-day Sallekhana, on 26 August 1955, he had a letter written and conferred the Acharya Pada upon his first nirgrantha (possessionless) disciple, Muni Shri Veersagar Ji. |
| Last discourse | On 8 September 1955, the 26th day of the 36-day Sallekhana, he gave his last discourse, in the Marathi language, for 22 minutes. |
| Passing away with Sallekhana | On Bhadrapada Shukla 2, 18 September 1955, at 6:50 in the morning, at Kunthalgiri Siddhakshetra in the province of Maharashtra, he left his body with Sallekhana. |

t: Charitra Chakravarti Shri 108 Shantisagar Question-Answer Quiz
grp: Charitra Chakravarti Shri 108 Shantisagar Question-Answer Quiz

c.b:
Shri Shantivirashivadharmajita "Vardhamana" Suribhyo Namah
(Salutations to the Acharyas Shanti, Vira, Shiva, Dharma, Ajita and "Vardhamana")

t: ** What was the birth-name of Acharya Shri Shantisagar Maharaj?

c.b: ** What was the birth-name of Acharya Shri Shantisagar Maharaj?
Satgauda Patil.

t: ** What was the name of Acharya Shri's father?

c.b: ** What was the name of Acharya Shri's father?
Bhimgauda Patil.

t: ** What was the name of Satgauda's mother?

c.b: ** What was the name of Satgauda's mother?
Satyavati.

t: ** Where was Satgauda born?

c.b: ** Where was Satgauda born?
At his maternal uncle's house, in Yelgul village, Maharashtra.

t: ** Which is Satgauda's ancestral village?

c.b: ** Which is Satgauda's ancestral village?
Bhojgram (Bhoj village).

t: ** When, and in which year, was Satgauda born?

c.b: ** When, and in which year, was Satgauda born?
On Ashadha Krishna 6, Vikram Samvat 1929, 1872 CE, on a Wednesday night.

t: * In which lineage (vansha*) and caste was Satgauda born?

c.b: * In which lineage (vansha*) and caste was Satgauda born?
In the Kshatriya lineage and the Chaturtha caste.

t: ** How many brothers did Satgauda have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many brothers did Satgauda have? Name them.
There were three brothers: Devgauda, Adigauda and Kumgauda.

t: ** How many sisters did Satgauda have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many sisters did Satgauda have? Name them.
There was one sister: Krishnabai.

t: ** When, and to whom, was Satgauda married?

c.b: ** When, and to whom, was Satgauda married?
At the age of 9, to a girl named Saraswati, aged 6.

t: ** When did Satgauda lose his wife?

c.b: ** When did Satgauda lose his wife?
Six months after the marriage.

t: ** What did the astrologer say on seeing Satgauda's horoscope?

c.b: ** What did the astrologer say on seeing Satgauda's horoscope?
"This child will be extremely religious. He will attain renown throughout the world, and will not get entangled in the affairs of the world."

t: ** How great was Satgauda's physical strength?

c.b: ** How great was Satgauda's physical strength?

He would easily lift a sack of four maunds of rice; he would draw water from the well using the mot (large leather bucket); with both feet together he would leap across a stretch twelve hasta (cubits) long; and he could knock down six men at once.

t: * What longing (dohala*) arose in his mother while Satgauda was in her womb?

c.b: * What longing (dohala*) arose in his mother while Satgauda was in her womb?
"May I worship Jinendra Bhagwan with one hundred and eight thousand-petalled lotuses."

t: ** From where were the lotus flowers procured?

c.b: ** From where were the lotus flowers procured?
From the lake of the King of Kolhapur.

t: ** Which rivers had their confluence near Bhojgram?

c.b: ** Which rivers had their confluence near Bhojgram?
The Vedganga and the Dudhganga rivers.

t: ** Whom did Satgauda carry across the confluence of the rivers?

c.b: ** Whom did Satgauda carry across the confluence of the rivers?
The Munirajs who came to Bhojgram.

t: ** How did Satgauda carry the Munirajs across the river?

c.b: ** How did Satgauda carry the Munirajs across the river?
He would seat them on his shoulders and carry them across.

t: ** What was Satgauda's life like in childhood?

c.b: ** What was Satgauda's life like in childhood?

He remained calm in disposition, never quarrelled with anyone, did not play dirty games, and stayed away from worldly amusements. From the very beginning his inclination was toward dispassion (vitaraga).

t: ** How did Satgauda conduct himself toward society?

c.b: ** How did Satgauda conduct himself toward society?
He treated everyone — poor and rich alike — with equality.

t: ** What did Satgauda tell society regarding animals?

c.b: ** What did Satgauda tell society regarding animals?
"Never underfeed the animals; keep giving them food and water on time; do not tie them with a short rope; do not beat them with whips," and so on.

t: ** What was the name of Satgauda's grandfather, and for how many generations had the family held the right of Patil?

c.b: ** What was the name of Satgauda's grandfather, and for how many generations had the family held the right of Patil?
His grandfather's name was Girigauda, and the family had held the right of Patil for seven generations.

t: ** Who is a Patil, and what authority does he have?

c.b: ** Who is a Patil, and what authority does he have?
The Patil is the protector (headman) of the village, and he has the authority to punish an offender for up to one month.

t: ** How did Satgauda conduct his business?

c.b: ** How did Satgauda conduct his business?

He sat at a cloth shop, and did business with a detached attitude. "When one is going to leave the house and go out anyway, what is the use of absorption and attachment in this?" He conducted the work with an attitude of indifference.

t: ** What effect did Satgauda's instruction have on Rudrappa, a devotee of Vedanta?

c.b: ** What effect did Satgauda's instruction have on Rudrappa, a devotee of Vedanta?
He began to drink filtered water and stopped eating at night. Once, while Rudrappa was eating at night, Satgauda had shown him directly the moths and other creatures falling into his food.

t: ** What was his non-attachment in business like?

c.b: ** What was his non-attachment in business like?

When he sat at the shop and someone came to buy cloth, he would say: "If you want cloth, choose it to your own liking, measure and cut it with your own hands, and write it in the account book with your own hand."

t: ** From where did Satgauda's ancestors come to Bhojgram, and why?

c.b: ** From where did Satgauda's ancestors come to Bhojgram, and why?
There was the terrible oppression of Tipu Sultan in Bijapur district; therefore they loaded all their property onto carts drawn by eight bullocks and came from Saraddi village.

t: ** How did Satgauda show compassion toward birds?

c.b: ** How did Satgauda show compassion toward birds?

When birds came to eat grain in his field, far from driving them away, he made arrangements for water for them to drink as well. When the harvest ripened, the grain in his field was more than in the fields of others.

t: ** Among the Munis whom Satgauda carried across the river, who was the chief Muniraj?

c.b: ** Among the Munis whom Satgauda carried across the river, who was the chief Muniraj?
Muni 108 Shri Adisagar Ji of Borgaon.

t: ** What did Satgauda say to the Muniraj while carrying him across the river?

c.b: ** What did Satgauda say to the Muniraj while carrying him across the river?
"I am taking you across the river; you take me across the ocean of worldly existence (bhava-sagara)."

t: * When and where did Satgauda take the vow of ekashana* (eating once a day)?

c.b: * When and where did Satgauda take the vow of ekashana* (eating once a day)?
At Sammed Shikhar Ji, at the age of 32.

t: ** Where did Satgauda renounce ghee and oil?

c.b: ** Where did Satgauda renounce ghee and oil?
At Sammed Shikhar Ji.

t: * Whom did Satgauda carry on his shoulder to perform the vandana* of Sammed Shikhar Ji, and what inspiration did he receive from this?

c.b: * Whom did Satgauda carry on his shoulder to perform the vandana* of Sammed Shikhar Ji, and what inspiration did he receive from this?
He carried an old mother on his back and had her perform the vandana; from this he received a powerful inspiration to become a renunciant (tyagi).

t: * Whom did Satgauda help perform the vandana* of Rajgrihi?

c.b: * Whom did Satgauda help perform the vandana* of Rajgrihi?
He carried an old man on his back and had him perform the vandana.

t: * For how many years did Satgauda, while a householder, take ekantara ahara* (food on alternate days), and what did he take as food?

c.b: * For how many years did Satgauda, while a householder, take ekantara ahara* (food on alternate days), and what did he take as food?
For five years; and he took milk and rice.

t: ** How did Satgauda save the life of a frog?

c.b: ** How did Satgauda save the life of a frog?
A snake was about to eat a frog; Satgauda flung the lota (water pot) in his hand forcefully onto a rock and saved it.

t: ** When did Satgauda first come into contact with a snake?

c.b: ** When did Satgauda first come into contact with a snake?
While he was lying in the field, a snake put its head out of the ground, touched his neck again and again, and then went back into its hole.

t: ** Why was Satgauda not afraid even at the touch of the snake?

c.b: ** Why was Satgauda not afraid even at the touch of the snake?
Great souls are fearless from childhood.

t: ** When his parents told Satgauda to marry, what would he say?

c.b: ** When his parents told Satgauda to marry, what would he say?
"If you put too much pressure on me, I shall become a Muni."

t: * At what age did Satgauda take the vow of lifelong brahmacharya* (celibacy)?

c.b: * At what age did Satgauda take the vow of lifelong brahmacharya* (celibacy)?
At the age of sixteen.

t: ** What did the village people call Satgauda?

c.b: ** What did the village people call Satgauda?
Everyone called him "Appa" (grandfather/elder).

t: ** How was Satgauda at horse-riding and marksmanship?

c.b: ** How was Satgauda at horse-riding and marksmanship?

He was of the first rank in horsemanship. As for marksmanship — he had never taken a gun in his hand in his life; yet once, when marksmanship was being discussed in jest, he took aim with a gun with full concentration and pierced a coconut. After that he never touched a gun again.

t: ** Whom did Satgauda save from the noose of hanging, and how?

c.b: ** Whom did Satgauda save from the noose of hanging, and how?

Fifteen to twenty men used to come to Satgauda at night to hear the scriptures; among them Malgauda Patil also used to come. One day he did not come. Satgauda went looking for him to his field; there Malgauda had put the noose around his neck, but was still alive. Satgauda saved Malgauda from dying.

t: ** What was Satgauda's devotion to Munis like, and what did he say to his mother?

c.b: ** What was Satgauda's devotion to Munis like, and what did he say to his mother?
When nirgrantha Munirajs came to the settlement he would serve them greatly. He would say to his mother: "I too will become a Muni; I shall not stay here."

t: * From when did Satgauda's feelings of dispassion (vairagya*) begin?

c.b: * From when did Satgauda's feelings of dispassion (vairagya*) begin?
From the age of 17–18 he had the feelings for nirgrantha diksha.

t: ** Then what was it that prevented Satgauda from becoming a Muni sooner?

c.b: ** Then what was it that prevented Satgauda from becoming a Muni sooner?
Satgauda's father insisted: "As long as we are alive, stay at home and practise Dharma." To obey his father's command he had to remain at home.

t: ** The Muni Maharaj whom Satgauda carried across the river — Adisagar Maharaj — after how many days used he to take food?

c.b: ** The Muni Maharaj whom Satgauda carried across the river — Adisagar Maharaj — after how many days used he to take food?
He took food after seven days; on the remaining days he fasted.

t: ** What did Muni Adisagar Maharaj take as food?

c.b: ** What did Muni Adisagar Maharaj take as food?
He took only one item in his food. When he took sugarcane juice, he took no other substance apart from it.

t: ** When Muni Adisagar Ji came to Bhojgram, where did he stay, and where did he live on other days?

c.b: ** When Muni Adisagar Ji came to Bhojgram, where did he stay, and where did he live on other days?
When he came to Bhoj he stayed only in Satgauda's shop and slept there that day; on other days he lived in the forest.

t: ** What was the cause of Satgauda's dispassion?

c.b: ** What was the cause of Satgauda's dispassion?
The impressions (samskara) of previous births.

t: * From whom did Satgauda take Kshullaka diksha*?

c.b: * From whom did Satgauda take Kshullaka diksha*?
From Muni Shri Devendrakirti Maharaj.

t: * Where did Satgauda take Kshullaka diksha*?

c.b: * Where did Satgauda take Kshullaka diksha*?
In Uttur village.

t: * When did he take Kshullaka diksha*?

c.b: * When did he take Kshullaka diksha*?
On Jyeshtha Shukla 13 (Trayodashi), Shaka Samvat 1837, 1916 CE, V.S. 1972.

t: ** Where was his first chaturmas as a Kshullaka?

c.b: ** Where was his first chaturmas as a Kshullaka?
In Kognoli village.

t: ** What was Satgauda's name after becoming a Kshullaka?

c.b: ** What was Satgauda's name after becoming a Kshullaka?
Kshullaka Shanti Sagar.

t: * How long after the samadhi (passing) of Satgauda's father did he take Kshullaka diksha*?

c.b: * How long after the samadhi (passing) of Satgauda's father did he take Kshullaka diksha*?
Four years later.

t: * How old was Satgauda when he took Kshullaka diksha*?

c.b: * How old was Satgauda when he took Kshullaka diksha*?
About forty-one years.

t: * After Kshullaka diksha, what was he given in place of a kamandalu (water-vessel), and where did he obtain a kamandalu*?

c.b: * After Kshullaka diksha, what was he given in place of a kamandalu (water-vessel), and where did he obtain a kamandalu*?
In place of a kamandalu he was given a lota (small water pot). In Kagal village a devout shravaka presented him with a kamandalu.

t: * Can a person of right faith (samyagdrishti) take recourse to false (mithya*) mantras, as one takes medicine, for curing disease?

c.b: * Can a person of right faith (samyagdrishti) take recourse to false (mithya*) mantras, as one takes medicine, for curing disease?

Maharaj Ji said: "There is no objection to taking medicine, for in medicine there is neither right faith nor wrong faith. But to accomplish one's purpose through mantras that involve the worship of false deities is to place faith in mithyatva (wrong belief); it would be a glorification of mithyatva. Therefore one should not take recourse to them."

t: * Where did Maharaj have the shravakas remove the idols of false deities (kudeva*) from their homes?

c.b: * Where did Maharaj have the shravakas remove the idols of false deities (kudeva*) from their homes?
In Jainbadi.

t: ** What was the second incident at Jainbadi?

c.b: ** What was the second incident at Jainbadi?
A Jain shravaka used to remove snake-poison with mithya mantras. The Jain brothers there said: "Do not make him give up his mithyatva."

t: ** What did Maharaj say to the Jain brothers of Jainbadi?

c.b: ** What did Maharaj say to the Jain brothers of Jainbadi?
"We shall give him another mantra." He had him give up mithyatva for two months and gave him a mantra.

t: ** What was the effect of that mantra?

c.b: ** What was the effect of that mantra?

A bullock had been bitten by a snake. By that mantra the snake's venom was removed at once; and the Jain brother reported that by this mantra other terrible diseases also went away. He gave up mithyatva for ever.

t: * Where did Kshullaka Shantisagar take Ailaka diksha*?

c.b: * Where did Kshullaka Shantisagar take Ailaka diksha*?
At Girnar Ji, the nirvana-bhumi (place of liberation) of Bhagwan Neminath.

t: ** With whom did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji go to Girnar Ji?

c.b: ** With whom did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji go to Girnar Ji?
With the shravakas of Samdoli.

t: ** By what means did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji go to Girnar Ji?

c.b: ** By what means did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji go to Girnar Ji?
He went to Girnar Ji by train.

t: ** Where did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji renounce vehicles?

c.b: ** Where did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji renounce vehicles?
At Kundal station near Sangli he got down from the train, had darshan of the temple, and renounced vehicles for ever.

t: * At Girnar Ji, why did Ailaka Shantisagar Ji one day go into the chauka* (place of food-offering) for food and return without taking it?

c.b: * At Girnar Ji, why did Ailaka Shantisagar Ji one day go into the chauka* (place of food-offering) for food and return without taking it?

A sadhu must stop taking food 72 minutes (three ghadi) before evening. So little time remained that the food could not have been finished; hence, because of the possibility of a fault in the vow, he returned.

t: ** Where was Ailaka Shantisagar's first chaturmas?

c.b: ** Where was Ailaka Shantisagar's first chaturmas?
In Naslapur.

t: * If a sadhu does not obtain food on his first round (charya*), may he go out a second time?

c.b: * If a sadhu does not obtain food on his first round (charya*), may he go out a second time?
Having made the resolve to go out for food and then going out twice, the vow of a single meal becomes tainted. Therefore, going out only once — in the morning or after noon — is the path of Dharma.

t: ** Why did Kshullaka Shantisagar not obtain food for many days?

c.b: ** Why did Kshullaka Shantisagar not obtain food for many days?

In those days the Jain priest (upadhyaya) used to fix the place in advance at a householder's home, and the sadhus used to go there. In this there arose the fault of uddishta ahara (food prepared specifically for the recipient). He (Shantisagar) used to set out for charya from the temple. No one knew the (proper) method; therefore for many days he did not obtain food.

t: * Where was the parasmani* (philosopher's stone) in the navel of the image of Bhagwan Parshvanath, and where did it go afterwards?

c.b: * Where was the parasmani* (philosopher's stone) in the navel of the image of Bhagwan Parshvanath, and where did it go afterwards?

In Baba Nagar, an upadhyaya used at first, in times of distress, to make gold from it occasionally. After his death, his son made gold in a single day by touching many iron rods to it. Someone (then) took the paras away.

t: * When did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji take Ailaka diksha*?

c.b: * When did Kshullaka Shantisagar Ji take Ailaka diksha*?
On Pausha Shukla 14 (Chaudas).

t: * How many times did a snake inflict upasarga* (affliction) on Shantisagar Ji while he was a Kshullaka?

c.b: * How many times did a snake inflict upasarga* (affliction) on Shantisagar Ji while he was a Kshullaka?
Twice.

t: * From whom did Shantisagar Ji take Muni diksha*?

c.b: * From whom did Shantisagar Ji take Muni diksha*?
From Shri Devendra Kirti Ji Maharaj.

t: * When did Shantisagar Maharaj take Muni diksha*?

c.b: * When did Shantisagar Maharaj take Muni diksha*?
On Phalguna Shukla 14 (Chaturdashi), Vikram Samvat 1976, 1920 CE.

t: * Where did Shantisagar Maharaj take Muni diksha*?

c.b: * Where did Shantisagar Maharaj take Muni diksha*?
In Yarnal village, Belgaum district, Karnataka province.

t: ** Where was Muni Shantisagar Maharaj's first chaturmas?

c.b: ** Where was Muni Shantisagar Maharaj's first chaturmas?
In Kognoli village.

t: * In Kognoli village, who inflicted upasarga* on Muni Shantisagar Ji, and how?

c.b: * In Kognoli village, who inflicted upasarga* on Muni Shantisagar Ji, and how?
A madman, by throwing bricks and stones.

t: * Which festival was going on in Yarnal village at the time of Shantisagar Ji's Muni diksha*?

c.b: * Which festival was going on in Yarnal village at the time of Shantisagar Ji's Muni diksha*?
The Panchakalyanak Mahotsav of Bhagwan Chandraprabha was being held with great splendour.

t: * What happened after Muni Shantisagar Ji's diksha*?

c.b: * What happened after Muni Shantisagar Ji's diksha*?
Because the water in Yarnal had become contaminated, disease spread; for one month his body became extremely emaciated on account of fever.

t: ** How was Muni Shantisagar Ji's illness relieved?

c.b: ** How was Muni Shantisagar Ji's illness relieved?
The devout shravakas of Naslapur came and rendered great vaiyavritya (service to the ascetic).

t: ** In Kognoli village, what happened on the way while going for food, and what did he do?

c.b: ** In Kognoli village, what happened on the way while going for food, and what did he do?
On the way there was the house of a Brahmin (vipra). He objected in abusive language to their passing in front of his house. They changed their route of coming and going.

t: ** Where was Muni Shantisagar Ji's second chaturmas?

c.b: ** Where was Muni Shantisagar Ji's second chaturmas?
In Naslapur.

t: ** What incident took place with Muni Shantisagar Ji at Ainapur?

c.b: ** What incident took place with Muni Shantisagar Ji at Ainapur?

A shravaka, by mistake, received him for food (padgahan). That day pure food had not been prepared in his house. Very discreetly he brought the food-materials from the neighbouring house and offered the food, not letting Maharaj know.

t: ** When Shantisagar Ji learnt that the food offered had been brought from another's house, what did he do?

c.b: ** When Shantisagar Ji learnt that the food offered had been brought from another's house, what did he do?
As expiation (prayashchitta), in the month of Jyeshtha, at midday, he went and began meditating on a rock scorched by the fierce rays of the sun.

t: ** How much older was Devgauda than Satgauda, and what was his name after becoming a Muni?

c.b: ** How much older was Devgauda than Satgauda, and what was his name after becoming a Muni?
He was 9 years and 10 days older, and as a Muni his name was Vardhamansagar Maharaj.

t: * How many times did snakes inflict upasarga* on you (Acharya Shri) during your ascetic life?

c.b: * How many times did snakes inflict upasarga* on you (Acharya Shri) during your ascetic life?
Five times.

t: * Where did the greatest upasarga* by a snake take place?

c.b: * Where did the greatest upasarga* by a snake take place?
In Kognoli (Karnataka).

t: * In Kognoli, for how long did the snake inflict upasarga* on Shantisagar Maharaj, and how large was it?

c.b: * In Kognoli, for how long did the snake inflict upasarga* on Shantisagar Maharaj, and how large was it?
It remained coiled around him for two hours, and it was eight feet long.

t: ** Where was Acharya Shri's chaturmas of 1923, and how many caves were there?

c.b: ** Where was Acharya Shri's chaturmas of 1923, and how many caves were there?
In Konnur village. There were seven hundred caves there.

t: ** When Shantisagar Maharaj was made to take food brought from another's house, what else did he do besides meditating on the hot rock?

c.b: ** When Shantisagar Maharaj was made to take food brought from another's house, what else did he do besides meditating on the hot rock?
For eight days he took nothing in his food except milk.

t: * While meditating in the cave at Konnur, who inflicted upasarga* on Acharya Shri?

c.b: * While meditating in the cave at Konnur, who inflicted upasarga* on Acharya Shri?
A snake climbed up onto his body.

t: ** In the Konnur cave, for how long did the snake remain near Acharya Shri, and at what time of day did this occur?

c.b: ** In the Konnur cave, for how long did the snake remain near Acharya Shri, and at what time of day did this occur?
There the snake remained for three hours, and this happened in the afternoon.

t: * When Acharya Shri was asked about the upasarga* by the snake — "Were you not afraid?" — what did he say?

c.b: * When Acharya Shri was asked about the upasarga* by the snake — "Were you not afraid?" — what did he say?

"At the time of calamity we never felt fear or panic. We did not even feel the snake, because at that time our attention was fixed on Siddha Bhagwan. The snake came onto the body, coiled itself, and went away. What is there of importance in this?"

t: * Where did the upasarga* by a snake on Kshullaka Shantisagar Maharaj take place?

c.b: * Where did the upasarga* by a snake on Kshullaka Shantisagar Maharaj take place?
In the ancient Jain temple of Kognoli.

t: * Where else did a snake inflict upasarga* on Shantisagar Maharaj?

c.b: * Where else did a snake inflict upasarga* on Shantisagar Maharaj?
In Shedwal village.

t: * Where did a large ant (makoda) inflict upasarga* on Shantisagar Maharaj, and how?

c.b: * Where did a large ant (makoda) inflict upasarga* on Shantisagar Maharaj, and how?
In the forest of Konnur a large ant clung to his male organ and sucked blood; blood was flowing out.

t: * For how long did the upasarga* by the ant continue?

c.b: * For how long did the upasarga* by the ant continue?
For an hour and a half.

t: * Where did the upasarga* by ants on Acharya Shantisagar Maharaj take place, and for how long?

c.b: * Where did the upasarga* by ants on Acharya Shantisagar Maharaj take place, and for how long?
In a temple in the forest, for the whole night.

t: ** What happened when Acharya Shri's guru Devendra Kirti Ji was coming from Gokak town to Konnur?

c.b: ** What happened when Acharya Shri's guru Devendra Kirti Ji was coming from Gokak town to Konnur?

As it took longer than expected, night fell on the way in the forest. After performing the evening samayika, both Maharajs — Devendrakirti Ji and Aganya Pandit — went within a line drawn (on the ground). At night a lion came, but it could not enter within that line, and went away.

t: ** Where else did a snake come upon Acharya Shri?

c.b: ** Where else did a snake come upon Acharya Shri?
While he was meditating in a cave in the forest, a thick snake 12–13 feet long spread its hood and stood before his face.

t: * How did the upasarga* by ants occur?

c.b: * How did the upasarga* by ants occur?

Through the carelessness of the priest, while pouring oil into the lamp some oil fell on the ground, whereby ants came, and all night long they kept biting the lower part of Acharya Shri's body, the buttocks etc., and blood began to flow from the body.

t: * How many pages of the Agam scriptures did Shantisagar Maharaj study (swadhyaya*) every day?

c.b: * How many pages of the Agam scriptures did Shantisagar Maharaj study (swadhyaya*) every day?
He studied fifty pages.

t: ** Which subject did Acharya Shri say should be known first?

c.b: ** Which subject did Acharya Shri say should be known first?
"First one should have knowledge of karma-bandha (the bondage of karma); not Samayasara first."

t: * Why did Acharya Shri say that knowledge of karma-bandha* should come first?

c.b: * Why did Acharya Shri say that knowledge of karma-bandha* should come first?
"Only when there is knowledge of bondage can there be knowledge of moksha (liberation). Only when we know for what reason we have fallen into suffering shall we make the effort to escape from it."

t: ** Who gave hot milk into Maharaj's hands, and what happened to Acharya Shri as a result?

c.b: ** Who gave hot milk into Maharaj's hands, and what happened to Acharya Shri as a result?
A shravaka gave very hot milk as food, from which Maharaj fainted and fell to the ground at once.

t: ** In which village did Maharaj have the throat ailment, and what else happened there?

c.b: ** In which village did Maharaj have the throat ailment, and what else happened there?

In Kavlana there was pain in the throat. He had given up grain. He took food on alternate days. Because of continuous obstruction (antaraya) he once took food after six days. The body became emaciated. The severity of the cold increased. At night there was a violent fit of coughing; the breath that went out with it did not return for some time. The pulse also stopped, and the body became inert.

t: ** Where did a lion first come near Maharaj?

c.b: ** Where did a lion first come near Maharaj?
While he was meditating in the caves of Gokak village.

t: ** After Gokak, how many times did a lion come near Acharya Shri, and where?

c.b: ** After Gokak, how many times did a lion come near Acharya Shri, and where?
At Muktagiri, Shravanabelagola, Dronagiri and Sonagiri; and several times in the lonely forest on the way from Muktagiri to Badwani.

t: ** Who conferred the Acharya Pada on Muni Shantisagar Maharaj, where and when?

c.b: ** Who conferred the Acharya Pada on Muni Shantisagar Maharaj, where and when?
The fourfold Sangha conferred it at Samdoli (Maharashtra), on Ashwina Shukla Ekadashi, a Wednesday, Samvat 1981, 1924 CE.

t: * On the day Shantisagar Maharaj was given the Acharya Pada, to whom did he give Muni diksha*?

c.b: * On the day Shantisagar Maharaj was given the Acharya Pada, to whom did he give Muni diksha*?
He gave Muni diksha to Kshullaka Veersagar Ji and to Nemisagar Maharaj.

t: * When was Veersagar Ji given Kshullaka diksha*?

c.b: * When was Veersagar Ji given Kshullaka diksha*?
On Phalguna Shukla Saptami, V.S. 1980.

t: * What was Nemisagar Ji's name before he took Muni diksha*?

c.b: * What was Nemisagar Ji's name before he took Muni diksha*?
Shri Nemanna.

t: * Where was Acharya Shantisagar Maharaj given the title Charitra Chakravarti*?

c.b: * Where was Acharya Shantisagar Maharaj given the title Charitra Chakravarti*?
At Gajpantha Siddhakshetra.

t: ** When Maharaj was having the idols of other deities loaded onto carts in Jainbadi and immersed in the river, the king asked the reason; what did Maharaj say?

c.b: ** When Maharaj was having the idols of other deities loaded onto carts in Jainbadi and immersed in the river, the king asked the reason; what did Maharaj say?

"Just as, in your tradition, in the month of Bhadrapada, after the work is done, you immerse the Ganapati idols in the river — in the same way the period of worship of these has ended, so we too are immersing them in the river."

t: * Why does the Jain viewpoint forbid mithyatva*? What did Maharaj say on this subject?

c.b: * Why does the Jain viewpoint forbid mithyatva*? What did Maharaj say on this subject?
"Innocent people, out of ignorance, give the names of gods and goddesses to countless false things and, worshipping them, destroy their priceless human birth."

t: ** When did Acharya Shantisagar Maharaj, with the Sangha, make the pilgrimage to Shravanabelagola?

c.b: ** When did Acharya Shantisagar Maharaj, with the Sangha, make the pilgrimage to Shravanabelagola?

t: ** In South India, the Sangha of Acharya Shri Shantisagar Maharaj accepted food only from those whom it had made give up what?

c.b: ** In South India, the Sangha of Acharya Shri Shantisagar Maharaj accepted food only from those whom it had made give up what?
From those whom it had made give up mithyatva.

t: ** Why did Acharya Shri travel toward North India?

c.b: ** Why did Acharya Shri travel toward North India?
To put an end to the growing laxity in conduct (shithilachara) in the Jain community.

t: ** When did Acharya Shri's Sangha set out toward North India?

c.b: ** When did Acharya Shri's Sangha set out toward North India?
On Margashirsha Krishna Pratipada, saying "Om Namah Siddhebhyah."

t: ** Apart from Acharya Shri, how many Munis were with him? Name them.

c.b: ** Apart from Acharya Shri, how many Munis were with him? Name them.
There were three Munis: Muni Shri Nemisagar Ji, Veersagar Ji and Anantkirti Ji.

t: ** How many Ailakas were with Acharya Shri on the northward journey, and from where?

c.b: ** How many Ailakas were with Acharya Shri on the northward journey, and from where?
There were three Ailakas (all three named Payasagar), from Ainapur, Gokak and Shivapur.

t: ** How many Kshullakas were with Acharya Shri?

c.b: ** How many Kshullakas were with Acharya Shri?
Three: Mallisagar, Payasagar and Anantkirti.

t: ** How many Kshullikas were in the Sangha at the time of the northward journey?

c.b: ** How many Kshullikas were in the Sangha at the time of the northward journey?
Three: Shantimati, Chandramati and Anantmati.

t: ** At the start of the northward journey, how many shravakas and shravikas were with Acharya Shri?

c.b: ** At the start of the northward journey, how many shravakas and shravikas were with Acharya Shri?
About 200 shravakas, shravikas and ascetics (sadhu-sadhvi).

t: * Who was the sanghapati* (leader/organiser) of Acharya Shri's Sangha?

c.b: * Who was the sanghapati* (leader/organiser) of Acharya Shri's Sangha?
Seth Poonam Chand Ghasilal of Bombay.

t: ** What did Acharya Shri do to end laxity of conduct in North India?

c.b: ** What did Acharya Shri do to end laxity of conduct in North India?
The Sangha adopted this rule: it would accept food only from those who had given up unfiltered water and would take maryadit (restricted, within-limit) food together with purity of food and drink.

t: * From where did Acharya Shri's Sangha begin (shubharambha*) its journey to the north (Shikhar Ji)?

c.b: * From where did Acharya Shri's Sangha begin (shubharambha*) its journey to the north (Shikhar Ji)?
From Kumbhoj Bahubali (Maharashtra).

t: ** On which day did Acharya Shri's Sangha reach Sammed Shikhar Ji?

c.b: ** On which day did Acharya Shri's Sangha reach Sammed Shikhar Ji?
On Phalguna Shukla Tritiya, 1927.

t: ** When was the Panchakalyanak held at Sammed Shikhar Ji in the presence of Acharya Shri?

c.b: ** When was the Panchakalyanak held at Sammed Shikhar Ji in the presence of Acharya Shri?
In Phalguna of 1928.

t: ** Who sponsored this Panchakalyanak by his donation?

c.b: ** Who sponsored this Panchakalyanak by his donation?
Seth Pooran Sah Ji of Seoni.

t: ** About how many men and women attended the Shikhar Ji Panchakalyanak?

c.b: ** About how many men and women attended the Shikhar Ji Panchakalyanak?
About more than one lakh men and women from all over India.

t: ** Where was Acharya Shri's first chaturmas in North India?

c.b: ** Where was Acharya Shri's first chaturmas in North India?
At Katni, district Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh).

t: * Where did Acharya Shri perform the Simha Nishkridita* vow?

c.b: * Where did Acharya Shri perform the Simha Nishkridita* vow?
During the Lalitpur chaturmas.

t: * How many times did Acharya Shri perform the Simha Nishkridita* austerity?

c.b: * How many times did Acharya Shri perform the Simha Nishkridita* austerity?
Three times.

t: ** How many fasts did Acharya Shri perform in his lifetime?

c.b: ** How many fasts did Acharya Shri perform in his lifetime?
9,938 fasts.

t: ** Of Acharya Shri's 35 years as a Muni, how many days were spent in fasting?

c.b: ** Of Acharya Shri's 35 years as a Muni, how many days were spent in fasting?
27 years and 2 months were spent in fasting.

t: * How many Muni dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer at Sonagiri?

c.b: * How many Muni dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer at Sonagiri?
Four Muni dikshas.

t: * On which day did Acharya Shri confer Muni diksha* at Sonagiri?

c.b: * On which day did Acharya Shri confer Muni diksha* at Sonagiri?
On Agahan (Margashirsha) Shukla Purnima, at nine in the morning.

t: * To whom did Acharya Shri give Muni diksha* at Sonagiri?

c.b: * To whom did Acharya Shri give Muni diksha* at Sonagiri?
To the four Ailakas Shri Chandrasagar Ji, Payasagar Ji, Parshvakirti Ji and Nemisagar Ji. Parshvakirti Ji was named Muni Kunthusagar, and the others retained the same names.

t: * How long did Acharya Shri do japa* (mantra-recitation) in 24 hours?

c.b: * How long did Acharya Shri do japa* (mantra-recitation) in 24 hours?
From 9 at night till 7 in the morning; 3 hours at midday; and three hours in the evening.

t: * Why did Acharya Shri have people wear the yajnopavita* (sacred thread)?

c.b: * Why did Acharya Shri have people wear the yajnopavita* (sacred thread)?
"It is the symbol of the Ratnatraya (the Three Jewels). Only he is entitled to give charity and perform worship who has undergone the yajnopavita samskara."

t: * When Maharaj Ji was asked to accomplish (siddha*) a mantra, why did he refuse?

c.b: * When Maharaj Ji was asked to accomplish (siddha*) a mantra, why did he refuse?
"One with vows (vrati) does not bow to one without vows. To accomplish a vidya or a deity, bowing is necessary."

t: * What hardship (parishaha*) did Acharya Shri have to bear while going to Badwani?

c.b: * What hardship (parishaha*) did Acharya Shri have to bear while going to Badwani?
In the month of Jyeshtha, after the midday samayika, he walked daily on a hot tar road.

t: ** How did Acharya Shri save the life of Br. Jindas?

c.b: ** How did Acharya Shri save the life of Br. Jindas?
A white mark of leprosy had appeared on his forehead. He wanted to commit suicide. Acharya Shri consoled him and told him to recite the Ekibhava Stotra with purity. By that his disease was cured.

t: ** Where in Delhi did Acharya Shri travel with the Sangha?

c.b: ** Where in Delhi did Acharya Shri travel with the Sangha?
He travelled to New Delhi, the Red Fort, the Jama Masjid, the Viceroy's House and other places.

t: * How did Acharya Shri preserve the Siddhanta* scriptures?

c.b: * How did Acharya Shri preserve the Siddhanta* scriptures?
He had the Siddhanta scriptures engraved on copper plates.

t: ** In which states did Acharya Shri's Sangha travel?

c.b: ** In which states did Acharya Shri's Sangha travel?
In Maharashtra, Karnataka, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat and other provinces.

t: * Why has Acharya Shri been called Gurunam Guru* (the Guru of Gurus)?

c.b: * Why has Acharya Shri been called Gurunam Guru* (the Guru of Gurus)?
Because his diksha-guru Devendrasagar Ji, on experiencing faults in his own vows, took diksha afresh from Acharya Shri as expiation.

t: * How many japas of the Namokar Mantra* did Acharya Shri perform?

c.b: * How many japas of the Namokar Mantra* did Acharya Shri perform?
He performed eighteen crore japas.

t: * When a crisis befell the Dharma, how many japas* did he perform?

c.b: * When a crisis befell the Dharma, how many japas* did he perform?
He performed an anushthana of one and a quarter lakh japas.

t: * Where are the Siddhanta* scriptures engraved on copper plates?

c.b: * Where are the Siddhanta* scriptures engraved on copper plates?
In Phaltan town.

t: * Which Siddhanta* scriptures did Acharya Shri have preserved?

c.b: * Which Siddhanta* scriptures did Acharya Shri have preserved?
The Dhavala, Jayadhavala and Mahadhavala.

t: ** When was the Jaipur chaturmas of Acharya Shri's Sangha?

c.b: ** When was the Jaipur chaturmas of Acharya Shri's Sangha?
The fifth chaturmas in Rajasthan was at Jaipur in 1932.

t: * What upasarga* did Acharya Shri face in Jaipur, and where?

c.b: * What upasarga* did Acharya Shri face in Jaipur, and where?
At Khaniya Ji, Jaipur, one day someone shut the door of his room. The passage for air to go out and come in was closed. Acharya Shri fainted from suffocation.

t: * When did Acharya Shri renounce grain (anna*)?

c.b: * When did Acharya Shri renounce grain (anna*)?
On 15 August 1948.

t: ** When did the Bombay High Court's verdict come, and what was it?

c.b: ** When did the Bombay High Court's verdict come, and what was it?

On 24 July 1951 the verdict came that there is a difference in fundamentals between Jains and Hindus. Jain temples cannot be Hindu temples. Hence followers of other religions have no right to enter them without asking.

t: ** When did Acharya Shri begin taking grain again as food?

c.b: ** When did Acharya Shri begin taking grain again as food?
On 16 August 1951, the day of Raksha Bandhan.

t: ** After how many days did Acharya Shri take grain as food, and where?

c.b: ** After how many days did Acharya Shri take grain as food, and where?
After 1,105 days, in the pandal at Baramati.

t: ** What did Acharya Shri say the day before he took food?

c.b: ** What did Acharya Shri say the day before he took food?
"We have no worry about ourselves; but thousands of people have made renunciations on our account. Out of consideration for them, we shall take grain as food tomorrow."

t: ** What did Acharya Shri say about the poor and the suffering?

c.b: ** What did Acharya Shri say about the poor and the suffering?
"Remove the distress of the poor and the suffering; give food to the hungry; educate them."

t: ** When did Acharya Shri go into the forest to meditate?

c.b: ** When did Acharya Shri go into the forest to meditate?
He went on the days of Ashtami and Chaturdashi.

t: ** What did Acharya Shri say about an untoward event, and what untoward event occurred?

c.b: ** What did Acharya Shri say about an untoward event, and what untoward event occurred?
Acharya Shri had said that some calamity would soon befall the country; just four days later Gandhi Ji was assassinated.

t: ** For how many days in succession did Acharya Shri not receive water in his food?

c.b: ** For how many days in succession did Acharya Shri not receive water in his food?
For ten days in succession he did not receive water.

t: ** Who made an attempt on the lives of the Acharya Sangha, where and when?

c.b: ** Who made an attempt on the lives of the Acharya Sangha, where and when?
A person named Chhidi did so in Rajkheda village, on 11 February 1930.

t: ** What directions did Acharya Shri give to society?

c.b: ** What directions did Acharya Shri give to society?

He directed the opening of gurukulas, educational institutions, Jain pathshalas, orphanages, Jinavani (scripture) publishing institutions, and the like; and the prohibition of remarriage (of widows), inter-caste marriage and child marriage, etc.

t: * Where and how did the samadhi* of Anant Kirti Maharaj occur?

c.b: * Where and how did the samadhi* of Anant Kirti Maharaj occur?

In Morena. It was the cold season. A devotee placed a burning brazier (sigadi) in his room and shut the room. Maharaj had epilepsy; he fell down unconscious and his foot went into the brazier. The blood that flowed from the foot put out the fire, but a few days later he attained samadhi.

t: * What is the rule (shasana*) of the Acharya Parameshthi like?

c.b: * What is the rule (shasana*) of the Acharya Parameshthi like?
It is the rule of the Vitaraga (the Passionless One).

t: * What is the life-breath (prana) of the sadhus*?

c.b: * What is the life-breath (prana) of the sadhus*?
The Agam.

t: * How many Muni dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer?

c.b: * How many Muni dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer?
26 Muni dikshas.

t: * Name the nirgrantha* Muni disciples of Acharya Shri.

c.b: * Name the nirgrantha* Muni disciples of Acharya Shri.

108 Muni Shri Veersagar Ji, Nemisagar Ji [Nemappa Ji (of Kudchi)], Chandrasagar Ji, Payasagar Ji, Nemisagar Ji (of Puntur), Kunthusagar Ji, Dharmasagar Ji, Sudharmasagar Ji, Adisagar Ji and Vardhamansagar Ji.

t: * To whom did Acharya Shri give the first Aryika diksha*?

c.b: * To whom did Acharya Shri give the first Aryika diksha*?
To Chandramati Mataji.

t: * How many Kshullaka dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer?

c.b: * How many Kshullaka dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer?
28 Kshullaka dikshas.

t: * How many Kshullika dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer?

c.b: * How many Kshullika dikshas* did Acharya Shri confer?
He conferred 14 Kshullika dikshas.

t: ** How many chaturmas did Acharya Shri complete?

c.b: ** How many chaturmas did Acharya Shri complete?
In all, 41 chaturmas.

t: ** Where was Acharya Shri's last chaturmas?

c.b: ** Where was Acharya Shri's last chaturmas?
At Kunthalgiri Siddhakshetra.

t: ** Where did Acharya Shri adopt the twelve-year Utkrishta Sallekhana, and on which day?

c.b: ** Where did Acharya Shri adopt the twelve-year Utkrishta Sallekhana, and on which day?
At Gajpantha Siddhakshetra, on the day of Vijaya Dashami.

t: ** To which 92-year-old Muni did Acharya Shri give Sallekhana?

c.b: ** To which 92-year-old Muni did Acharya Shri give Sallekhana?
To Muni Vardhamansagar Ji, his elder brother from householder life.

t: ** To whom did Acharya Shri give his own Acharya Pada?

c.b: ** To whom did Acharya Shri give his own Acharya Pada?
To his first Muni disciple, Shri Veersagar Ji Maharaj.

t: ** What message did Acharya Shri send to Muni Veersagar Ji?

c.b: ** What message did Acharya Shri send to Muni Veersagar Ji?
"Conduct yourself according to the Agam; attain samadhimarana as we have; and make a worthy disciple your successor."

t: ** For how many days did Acharya Shri's final Sallekhana continue?

c.b: ** For how many days did Acharya Shri's final Sallekhana continue?
For 35 days; samadhi occurred on the 36th day.

t: ** When did Acharya Shri give the Acharya Pada to Veersagar Ji?

c.b: ** When did Acharya Shri give the Acharya Pada to Veersagar Ji?
On 26 August 1955, a Friday, by letter.

t: ** Who wrote the letter, and what was he made to write in it?

c.b: ** Who wrote the letter, and what was he made to write in it?
Pandit Sumeruchandra Diwakar wrote it. Maharaj had him write: "Of our own accord and with satisfaction, we confer the Acharya Pada upon our first nirgrantha disciple, Veersagar."

t: * When did Acharya Shri take Yama Sallekhana* (Sallekhana unto death)?

c.b: * When did Acharya Shri take Yama Sallekhana* (Sallekhana unto death)?
On 14 August 1955.

t: ** When did Acharya Shri give his last discourse?

c.b: ** When did Acharya Shri give his last discourse?
On the 26th day of the Sallekhana, 6 September 1955, in the Marathi language.

t: ** For how long did Acharya Shri give his last discourse?

c.b: ** For how long did Acharya Shri give his last discourse?
For 22 minutes.

t: * At what age did Acharya Shri attain samadhi*?

c.b: * At what age did Acharya Shri attain samadhi*?
At the age of 84.

t: * When and where did Acharya Shri attain samadhi*?

c.b: * When and where did Acharya Shri attain samadhi*?
At Kunthalgiri Siddhakshetra on 18 September 1955, Bhadrapada Shukla 2, at 6:50 in the morning.

t: ** In his last discourse, what instruction did Acharya Shri give to those desiring happiness?

c.b: ** In his last discourse, what instruction did Acharya Shri give to those desiring happiness?
"Destroy Darshana Mohaniya (faith-deluding karma) and attain Samyaktva (right faith)."

t: * What did Acharya Shri say about samyama* (self-restraint) in his discourse?

c.b: * What did Acharya Shri say about samyama* (self-restraint) in his discourse?

"Do not fear samyama; adopt samyama. Without it there will be no welfare. Adopt samyama to destroy Charitra Mohaniya (conduct-deluding karma). Instead of going to hell you will at least go to heaven."

t: * What instruction was given about ahimsa* (non-violence), and what is the root of the Jain Dharma?

c.b: * What instruction was given about ahimsa* (non-violence), and what is the root of the Jain Dharma?
"The root of Dharma is compassion, ahimsa. Practise truth and ahimsa. Work is not accomplished by saying it with the mouth; the fruit is obtained by doing."

t: Pooja of Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Ji Mahamuniraj
grp: Pooja of Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Ji Mahamuniraj

c.b: Translator's note on this section: The Pooja is a devotional text meant for recitation. Each verse is therefore given first in Roman transliteration (so that it can be recited as in the original) and then in English meaning. The Sanskrit mantras that accompany each offering are given in transliteration, with the meaning of the recurring formula explained once.

t: Sthapana (Invocation) — to the tune of "Prabhu Patit Pavan"
grp: Sthapana (Invocation) — to the tune of "Prabhu Patit Pavan"

c.b:
He Shantisagar shantikarta, shanti ke datar ho.
Kalikal pancham manhi aakar, dharma ke kartar ho.
Charon gati mein bhraman kina, dukh sahe bharpur jo.
Ham sharan aaye nath teri, kasht sare door ho.
O Shantisagar, bringer of peace, giver of peace! Having come into this fifth age of Kali, you are the doer of Dharma. We who have wandered through the four states of existence and suffered pain in full — we have come to your refuge, O Lord; may all our troubles be removed.
Doha (couplet):
Aahvanan ham kar rahe, hriday virajo aay.
Paap karam sab nasht hon, bhav bhav hoy sahay.
We are making the invocation; come and be seated in our heart. May all sinful karmas be destroyed; be our helper in birth after birth.
Om Hreem Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo atra avatara avatara samvaushat — aahvananam. (Invocation: "O Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar, foremost of great ascetics, descend here, descend here.")
Om Hreem Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo atra tishtha tishtha thah thah — sthapanam. (Establishment: "…abide here, abide here.")
Om Hreem Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo atra mama sannihito bhava bhava vashat — sannidhikaranam. (Drawing near: "…be present close to me, be present.")

t: Ashtaka (The Eight Offerings) — Narendra metre

c.b:
Jala (Water)
Janam maran ko karte karte, kaal anant gamaye hain.
Aavagaman mita do Guruvar, jal bhar kalasha laye hain.
Shantisagar Ji mahatapasvi, mangalkari sukhadai.
Kalikal ka dosh mitakar, municharya ko batlai.
Being born and dying, again and again, we have let endless time pass. Remove our coming and going (transmigration), O great Guru — we have brought a kalasha filled with water. Shantisagar Ji, the great ascetic, the auspicious one, the giver of happiness, wiped away the blemish of the Kali age and showed the conduct of a Muni.
Om Hreem Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo janma-jara-mrityu-vinashanaya jalam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the destruction of birth, old age and death, I offer water.")
Chandana (Sandal-paste)
Bhavavan ki is maha anal mein, ab tak jalta aaya hoon.
Bhav ka taap mitado Guruvar, chandan charan chadhaya hoon. — Shantisagar.
In this great fire of the forest of worldly existence I have been burning until now. Remove the heat of samsara, O great Guru — I have offered sandal at your feet. — Shantisagar.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo samsara-taapa-vinashanaya chandanam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the destruction of the heat of samsara, I offer sandal.")
Akshata (Unbroken rice)
Koi bhi thir na is jag mein, kshan mein nashvar ho jaye.
Akshaya pad pane ke karan, akshat lekar ham aaye. — Shantisagar.
Nothing in this world is stable; in a moment it becomes perishable. To attain the imperishable state, we have come bringing unbroken rice. — Shantisagar.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo akshaya-pada-praptaye akshatan nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the attainment of the imperishable state, I offer unbroken rice.")
Pushpa (Flowers)
Maha tapasvi tap ke bal se, Kamadev ka mad chhina.
Kamabaan ke naash karan ko, pushpa charan mein dhar dina. — Shantisagar.
The great ascetic, by the power of his austerity, stripped Kamadeva (the god of desire) of his pride. To destroy the arrows of desire, I have placed flowers at your feet. — Shantisagar.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo kamabana-vidhvamsanaya pushpam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the destruction of the arrows of desire, I offer flowers.")
Naivedya (Food-offering)
Kshudha rog se peedit hokar, ab tak bahu dukh paye hain.
Kshudha dakini door bhagado, shatras vyanjan laye hain. — Shantisagar.
Afflicted by the disease of hunger, we have suffered much until now. Drive away the demoness of hunger — we have brought dishes of the six flavours. — Shantisagar.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo kshudha-roga-vinashanaya naivedyam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the destruction of the disease of hunger, I offer food.")
Deepa (Lamp)
Mithyatam se raah na dikhe, tav charanon mein aaye hain.
Gyan ujala karo hamara, deep jalakar laye hain. — Shantisagar.
In the darkness of mithyatva (false belief) we cannot see the path; we have come to your feet. Kindle the light of knowledge in us — we have brought a lit lamp. — Shantisagar.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo mohandhakara-vinashanaya deepam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the destruction of the darkness of delusion, I offer a lamp.")
Dhoopa (Incense)
Dasavidh dhoop anal mein khevoon, maha sugandhit laoonga.
Asht karam ki dhoom udakar, Shivramani pa jaoonga. — Shantisagar.
I offer ten-fold incense into the fire and bring great fragrance. Sending up the smoke of the eight karmas, I shall attain the Bride of Liberation (Shiva-ramani). — Shantisagar.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo ashtakarma-dahanaya dhoopam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the burning of the eight karmas, I offer incense.")
Phala (Fruit)
Nishphal ab tak bhatak raha hoon, raah kahin na payi hai.
Mahamoksha phal prapt karan ko, teri pooj rachai hai. — Shantisagar.
Fruitlessly I have wandered until now; nowhere have I found the path. To obtain the great fruit of moksha, I have composed this worship of you. — Shantisagar.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo moksha-phala-praptaye phalam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the attainment of the fruit of liberation, I offer fruit.")
Arghya (The combined offering)
Jal chandan akshat charu deepak, dhoop phool phal le aaye.
Asht dravya se pooj rachakar, Siddha shila ko pa javen.
Shantisagar Ji mahatapasvi, mangalkari sukhadai.
Kalikal ka dosh mitakar, municharya ko batlai.
Water, sandal, unbroken rice, food, lamp, incense, flowers and fruit — we have brought them. Composing this worship with the eight substances, may we attain the Siddha Shila (the abode of the liberated). Shantisagar Ji, the great ascetic, the auspicious one, the giver of happiness, wiped away the blemish of the Kali age and showed the conduct of a Muni.
Om Hreem … Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo anargha-pada-praptaye arghyam nirvapamiti svaha. ("…for the attainment of the priceless state, I offer arghya.")
Shanti-dhara (Stream of Peace)
Shanti dhara ham karen, shanti pane het.
Shanti Guru ke charan mein, pooja bhav samet. — Shantaye Shantidhara.
We pour the stream of peace for the attainment of peace, at the feet of the Guru of Peace, together with the feeling of worship. — The stream of peace, for peace.
Pushpanjali (Handful of flowers)
Nana vidhi ke suman le, deoon charan chadhay.
Prabhav bhakti teri kare, kamabaan nash jaay. — Divya Pushpanjali.
Taking flowers of many kinds, I offer them at your feet. May Prabhav (the composer) perform your devotion; may the arrows of desire be destroyed. — The divine handful of flowers.
Mantra: Om Hreem Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo namah (9 times).

t: Jayamala (Garland of Victory) — Chaupai metre

c.b:
Shantiguru tum ho hitkari, sab jeevon par karuna dhari.
Charon gati mein ghoom liya hai, tumne jag ka chhor liya hai.
Guru of Peace, you are the benefactor, bearing compassion for all living beings. You have wandered through the four states of existence; you have reached the far shore of the world.
Satyavati mata ur aaye, Bhimgaud ke tanuj kahaye.
Jo bhi muni nagari mein aate, kandhon se nadi paar karate.
You came into the womb of mother Satyavati and were called the son of Bhimgauda. Whatever Munis came to the town, you carried them across the river on your shoulders.
Phagun sudi chaudas jab aayi, municharya ban kar dikhlayi.
Ashubh yog na man mein aave, shubh yogon se dhyan lagave.
When Phalguna Shukla Chaturdashi came, you took up the Muni's conduct and showed it. No inauspicious activity entered your mind; you fixed your meditation through auspicious activities.
Teen ashubh leshya ab nahin, shubh leshya hi shesh rahai.
Nana upasarg sahe bahu bhari, apne man mein samata dhari.
The three inauspicious leshyas (colourings of the soul) were no more; only the auspicious leshyas remained. You bore many very heavy afflictions, holding equanimity in your mind.
Nagraj tum par chadh aaya, Simharaj se bhay nahin khaya.
Achal dhyan ke ho tum swami, samata ke sagar tum nami.
The king of serpents climbed upon you; you felt no fear of the king of lions. You are the master of unshakeable meditation; you are renowned as the ocean of equanimity.
Man mein khed ka nahin thikana, Shanti Sagar daya nidhana.
Nikat bhavya tum nath rahavo, alp kaal mein Shivpur pavo.
In your mind there was no trace of distress, O Shantisagar, treasure of compassion. O Lord, you are a nikata-bhavya (soul near to liberation); in a short time you will attain the City of Liberation.
Jeevan sara tap mein beeta, karam bali ko tumne jeeta.
Panchamkaal mahadukhadai, samyam ki charya batlai.
Your whole life passed in austerity; you conquered the mighty karma. In the fifth age, the giver of great sorrow, you showed the conduct of self-restraint.
Uttar dish mein tum na aate, kahin ek na sadhu paate.
Agam ke anukool bataya, kahin na usmein avgun paya.
Had you not come to the northern region, not a single sadhu would have been found anywhere. You taught in accordance with the Agam; no fault was ever found in it.
Simha samaan maha baldhari, hathi sam the unnat bhari.
Pavan samaan vicharne wale, roke se na rukne wale.
Mighty in strength like a lion, lofty and grand like an elephant; wandering like the wind, not to be stopped by any hindrance.
Meru sam tha dhyan tumhara, karma-shatru bhi tumse hara.
Surya samaan tej ke dhari, chandra-kiran sam sheetal bhari.
Your meditation was like Mount Meru; even the enemy karma was defeated by you. Bearer of brilliance like the sun, and cool like the rays of the moon.
Ashwin shubh Ekadashi aaya, Acharaj pad tumne paya.
Charitra-chakri aap kahaye, shat-avashyak hamen bataye.
The auspicious Ashwina Ekadashi came; you received the Acharya Pada. You were called the Charitra Chakravarti; you taught us the six essential duties (shad-avashyaka).
Goonga bole, langda chale, kushti apna kusht mitale.
Dukhiya jo charanon mein aaya, sankat uska door bhagaya.
The dumb spoke, the lame walked, the leper had his leprosy removed. Whoever came in distress to your feet — you drove his trouble far away.
Indriya panchon vash mein keeni, shatkayon ki raksha keeni.
Jin mandir par sankat aaya, Guruvar tumne use bachaya.
You brought the five senses under control; you protected the six classes of living beings. When a crisis came upon the Jain temples, O great Guru, you saved them.
Jinavani ki raksha keeni, tamrapatra par likhva deeni.
Ham sab tav charanon mein aaye, bhav sagar se ham tir jayen.
You protected the Jinavani (the word of the Jina); you had it written on copper plates. We have all come to your feet; may we cross the ocean of existence.
Doha:
Teen lok kagaj karoon, lekhani sab banaray.
Sab sagar syahi karoon, Guru gun likha na jaay.
Were I to make the three worlds my paper, all the forests my pens, and all the oceans my ink — still the virtues of the Guru could not be written.
Om Hreem Shri Charitra Chakravarti Acharya 108 Shri Shantisagar Mahayativarebhyo jayamala poornargham nirvapamiti svaha. ("…I offer the full arghya of the Jayamala.")
Doha:
Guruvar tere naam se, bigde bante kaam.
Prabhav hit badhta rahe, Shivpur mein ho dhaam.
O great Guru, by your name ruined works are set right. May the welfare of Prabhav (the composer) keep increasing; may his abode be in the City of Liberation.
Ityashirvadah — divya pushpanjalim kshipet. (Thus the benediction — cast the divine handful of flowers.)

t: Arghya to Charitra Chudamani Acharya 108 Shri Veersagar Ji Maharaj
grp: Arghya to Charitra Chudamani Acharya 108 Shri Veersagar Ji Maharaj

c.b:
Jal phal aathon dravya sajakar, swarna thaal bhar laye hain.
Bhav se paar laga do Guruvar, pooja paath rachaye hain.
Shanti Sindhu ne patta diya hai, pratham patta kahlate hain.
Path bhoole hain raah batado, charanan sheesh namate hain.
Arranging the eight substances — water, fruit and the rest — we have brought them heaped in a golden plate. Carry us across worldly existence, O great Guru; we have composed this worship. The Ocean of Peace (Shantisagar) gave you the seat (patta); you are called the first patta-holder. We have lost the path — show us the way; we bow our heads at your feet.
Om Hreem Charitra Chudamani Acharya Shri Veersagar Ji argham nirvapamiti svaha.

t: Arghya to Siddhanta Samrakshaka (Protector of the Doctrine) Acharya 108 Shri Shivsagar Ji Maharaj
grp: Arghya to Siddhanta Samrakshaka (Protector of the Doctrine) Acharya 108 Shri Shivsagar Ji Maharaj

c.b:
Panchachar ka palan karte, shishyon se karvate hain.
Nath aapke pad pankaj se, bhavsagar tir jate hain.
Shivsagar Guru Shiv ke rahi, Shiv ki raah bata dena.
Bhavsagar mein doob rahe, jag se paar laga dena.
You observe the fivefold conduct (panchachara) and have your disciples observe it. O Lord, by your lotus feet we cross the ocean of existence. Guru Shivsagar, traveller on the road to Liberation — show us the road to Liberation. We are drowning in the ocean of existence; carry us across the world.
Om Hreem Siddhanta Samrakshaka Acharya 108 Shri Shivsagar Ji argham nirvapamiti svaha.

t: Arghya to Dharma Shiromani Acharya 108 Shri Dharmasagar Ji Maharaj
grp: Arghya to Dharma Shiromani Acharya 108 Shri Dharmasagar Ji Maharaj

c.b:
Par ko ab tak mana maine, bhool anadi chhaya hai.
Nij mein nij ka gun pane ko, pooja paath rachaya hai.
Dharmasindhu Guru Dharmaveer ho, Dharma dhwaja ke dhari ho.
Tum ho bhole Baba Guruvar, sat sat naman hamari ho.
Until now I have taken the "other" (non-self) to be mine; a beginningless error has overshadowed me. To find the qualities of the self within the self, I have composed this worship. Guru, Ocean of Dharma, you are the hero of Dharma, the bearer of the banner of Dharma. You are the guileless "Baba," O great Guru; our salutations to you a hundred times over.
Om Hreem Dharma Shiromani 108 Acharya Shri Dharmasagar Ji argham nirvapamiti svaha.

t: Arghya to Abhikshna Gyanopayogi (Ever Engaged in Knowledge) Acharya 108 Shri Ajitsagar Ji Maharaj
grp: Arghya to Abhikshna Gyanopayogi (Ever Engaged in Knowledge) Acharya 108 Shri Ajitsagar Ji Maharaj

c.b:
Kaal anadi bhatke jag mein, raah kahin na payi hai.
Shivpur ki ab raah batado, charanan pooj rachai hai.
Bal brahmachari ho Guruvar, Kamdev ko mara hai.
Gyan dhyan tap leen tapasvi, Dharmasindhu patta dhara hai.
From beginningless time we have wandered in the world; nowhere have we found the path. Show us now the road to the City of Liberation — we have composed this worship at your feet. A celibate from childhood, O great Guru, you have slain Kamadeva. An ascetic absorbed in knowledge, meditation and austerity, you have held the seat (patta) of the Ocean of Dharma (Dharmasagar).
Om Hreem Abhikshna Gyanopayogi 108 Acharya Shri Ajitsagar Ji argham nirvapamiti svaha.

t: Arghya to Acharya-kalpa 108 Shri Shrutsagar Ji Maharaj
grp: Arghya to Acharya-kalpa 108 Shri Shrutsagar Ji Maharaj

c.b:
Teen lok ke sab phal khaye, Shiv phal ab tak paya nay.
Maha moksha-phal pane karan, argh chadhaoon Guru ke aay.
Veer Sindhu ke antim munivar, Shrutsagar Gurudev mahan.
Khyati laabh se door rahe ho, nahin liya Suri padmaan.
I have tasted all the fruits of the three worlds, but the fruit of Liberation I have not yet obtained. To gain the great fruit of moksha, I come and offer arghya to the Guru. Last of the Munis of the Ocean of Veer (Veersagar), great Gurudev Shrutsagar — you have stayed far from fame and gain; you did not accept the honour of the Acharya (Suri) Pada.
Om Hreem Acharya-kalpa 108 Shri Shrutsagar Ji argham nirvapamiti svaha.

t: Sthapana (Invocation)

c.b:
Panchachar ka palan karte, shishyon se karvate hain.
Agam path par chale nirantar, bhavsagar tirvate ho.
Poorab, Pashchim, Uttar, Dakshin, vrish phailaya jakar ke.
Aahvanan ham karen aapka, hriday virajo aakar ke.
You observe the fivefold conduct and have your disciples observe it. You walk continually on the path of the Agam and carry us across the ocean of existence. Going to the East, West, North and South, you have spread the Dharma (vrisha). We invoke you; come and be seated in our heart.
Om Hreem Shattrimshat-Gunamandita-Acharya Vatsalya Varidhi Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo atra avatara avatara samvaushat — aahvananam. (Invocation: "O Acharya adorned with the thirty-six virtues, Ocean of Affection, Shri Vardhamansagar, foremost of great ascetics, descend here, descend here.")
Om Hreem Shattrimshat-Gunamandita-Acharya Vatsalya Varidhi Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo atra tishtha tishtha thah thah — sthapanam.
Om Hreem Shattrimshat-Gunamandita-Acharya Vatsalya Varidhi Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo atra mama sannihito bhava bhava vashat — sannidhikaranam.

t: Ashtaka (The Eight Offerings)

c.b:
Jala (Water)
Prasuk karke jal le aaye, kanchan kalasha bharayenge.
Guru charanon mein dhara dekar, janam-maran nashayenge.
Path bhoole hain raah batado, pancham patta dhari ho.
Vartaman ke Vardhaman ko, shat shat naman hamaro ho.
Making the water pure (prasuka) we have brought it and filled a golden kalasha. Pouring a stream at the Guru's feet, we shall destroy birth and death. We have lost the path — show us the way, O holder of the fifth seat (patta). To the Vardhaman of the present age, our salutations a hundred times over.
Om Hreem Shattrimshat-Gunamandita-Acharya Vatsalya Varidhi Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo janma-jara-mrityu-vinashanaya jalam nirvapamiti svaha.
Chandana (Sandal)
Malayagiri ka chandan lekar, kesar sang ghisayenge.
Guru charanon ki pooj rachakar, bhav ka taap mitayenge. — Path bhoole hain…
Taking sandal of the Malaya mountain, we shall grind it with saffron. Composing the worship of the Guru's feet, we shall remove the heat of samsara. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo samsara-taapa-vinashanaya chandanam nirvapamiti svaha.
Akshata (Unbroken rice)
Chandra-kiran sam shwet manohar, akshat thaal bharayenge.
Akshaya-pad ke prapt karan ko, Guru charanon mein layenge. — Path bhoole hain…
We shall fill a plate with unbroken rice, white and lovely as moonbeams. To attain the imperishable state, we shall bring it to the Guru's feet. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo akshaya-pada-praptaye akshatan nirvapamiti svaha.
Pushpa (Flowers)
Kamal ketaki pushpa manohar, maha sugandhit laye hain.
Kamabaan ka naash karado, charanan bhent chadhaye hain. — Path bhoole hain…
Lovely lotus and ketaki flowers, greatly fragrant, we have brought. Destroy the arrows of desire — we have offered them as a gift at your feet. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo kamabana-vidhvamsanaya pushpam nirvapamiti svaha.
Naivedya (Food)
Ghevar pheni modak khaja, shuddh banakar laye hain.
Kshudha dakini naash karan ko, teri pooj rachaye hain. — Path bhoole hain…
Ghevar, pheni, modak and khaja (sweets), prepared pure, we have brought. To destroy the demoness of hunger, we have composed your worship. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo kshudha-roga-vinashanaya naivedyam nirvapamiti svaha.
Deepa (Lamp)
Manimay deep jalakar laye, aarti karne aaye hain.
Moha mahatam naash karado, yahi bhavna bhaye hain. — Path bhoole hain…
We have brought a lit jewelled lamp; we have come to perform aarti. Destroy the great darkness of delusion — this alone is the feeling we cherish. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo mohandhakara-vinashanaya deepam nirvapamiti svaha.
Dhoopa (Incense)
Das vidhi dhoop sugandhit lekar, agni manhi jalate hain.
Asht karm ki dhoom udado, tav charanon mein aate hain. — Path bhoole hain…
Taking fragrant ten-fold incense, we burn it in the fire. Send up the smoke of the eight karmas — we come to your feet. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo ashtakarma-dahanaya dhoopam nirvapamiti svaha.
Phala (Fruit)
Seb santra dadim kela, phal vivarjit laye hain.
Shivpur ki Guru raah dikhado, charanan pooj rachaye hain. — Path bhoole hain…
Apple, orange, pomegranate and banana — we have brought choice fruits. Show us, Guru, the road to the City of Liberation — we have composed the worship of your feet. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo mahamoksha-phala-praptaye phalam nirvapamiti svaha.
Arghya (Combined offering)
Jal phal aadik asht dravya le, kanchan thaal bharaye hain.
Maha moksha phal prapt karan ko, charan kamal mein aaye hain. — Path bhoole hain…
Taking the eight substances — water, fruit and the rest — we have filled a golden plate. To obtain the great fruit of moksha, we have come to your lotus feet. — We have lost the path…
Om Hreem … Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo anargha-pada-praptaye arghyam nirvapamiti svaha.
Shanti-dhara
Shantidhara ham karen, man mein ati harshaye.
Rog shok sankat mite, janam saphal ho jaye. — Shantaye Shantidhara.
We pour the stream of peace, with great joy in our hearts. May disease, sorrow and calamity vanish; may this birth become fruitful.
Pushpanjali
Nana vidhi ke suman le, sundar maal banay.
Pushpanjali arpan kare, kamabaan nash jaay. — Pushpanjali.
Taking flowers of many kinds, making a beautiful garland, we offer the handful of flowers; may the arrows of desire be destroyed.

t: Jayamala

c.b:
Doha:
Guru ki mahima agam hai, kaise karoon bakhan.
Bhakti ke vash ho raha, karta hoon yashgaan.
The glory of the Guru is unfathomable; how shall I describe it? Overcome by devotion, I sing his praise.
Yashwant bankar janm liya tha, ab yah bane yashasvi sant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne, karne ko bhav ka ab ant. ॥1॥
He was born as Yashwant; now he has become a renowned saint. He has set out to cut the karmas, to make an end of worldly existence now. (1)
Bhadav Shukla saate shubh din, Maha Sanavad nagar manjhar.
Kamalchand Ji pita aapke, ghar-ghar ho raha mangalachar.
Maa Manorama ke sut pyare, naam dharaya tha Yashwant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥2॥
On the auspicious day of Bhadrapada Shukla 7, in the town of Maha Sanavad — Kamalchand Ji was your father; in every home there were auspicious rites. Beloved son of mother Manorama, you were given the name Yashwant. He has set out to cut the karmas… (2)
Ashtadash ki bhai umra jab, aaye Shivsagar ke paas.
Diksha ki arji kar deeni, charanon mein aaya hai daas.
Shikhar Sammed Guru ne bheja, peechhe ho gaya Shiv ka ant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥3॥
When he reached the age of eighteen, he came to Shivsagar. He made his petition for diksha: "This servant has come to your feet." The Guru sent him to Shikhar Sammed; afterwards Shiv(sagar)'s end came. He has set out to cut the karmas… (3)
Dharma Sindhu se diksha leeni, parishaha sahe maha ghanghor.
Nainan jyoti chali gayi hai, chalta nahin kisi ka jor.
Shanti Prabhu ki bhakti keeni, nainan jyoti payi sant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥4॥
He took diksha from the Ocean of Dharma (Dharmasagar); he bore hardships most terrible. The light of his eyes went away; no one's power could avail. He performed the devotion of Lord Shanti(nath); the saint regained the light of his eyes. He has set out to cut the karmas… (4)
Ajit Suri ne patra likha hai, apna pattadhish banay.
Nar-nari sadhu bahu aaye, pancham patta-dhish kahay.
Nagar Parsola ke andar, sare sangh ke bane mahant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥5॥
Acharya Ajit(sagar) wrote a letter making him his successor on the seat. Men, women and many sadhus came; he was called the fifth holder of the seat. Within the town of Parsola he became the head of the whole Sangha. He has set out to cut the karmas… (5)
Pancha-mahavrat pancha-samiti, teen gupti palan karte.
Baees parishaha sahe nirantar, das-o-dharam dharan karte.
Barah bhavan bhave harpal, karam aavate roke sant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥6॥
He observes the five great vows, the five carefulnesses and the three restraints; he bears the twenty-two hardships continually and holds the ten Dharmas. Every moment he contemplates the twelve reflections; the saint stops the inflow of karma. He has set out to cut the karmas… (6)
Man indriya ko bas mein karli, chhahon kaay par raksha aay.
Panchachar ka palan karte, shishyon se palan karvay.
Dukhiya jo charanon mein aaya, sankat uska hara turant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥7॥
He has brought mind and senses under control, protecting the six classes of beings. He observes the fivefold conduct and has his disciples observe it. Whoever came in distress to his feet — his trouble was removed at once. He has set out to cut the karmas… (7)
Bahubali ke Bhattarak Ji, vinati aakar keeni hai.
Teer baar abhishek karaye, charanon drishti deeni hai.
Nana sangh vahan par aaye, sabhi sanghon ke bane mahant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥8॥
The Bhattarak Ji of Bahubali came and made a request; three times he had the abhisheka performed, and cast his gaze upon (the Guru's) feet. Many Sanghas came there; he became the head of all the Sanghas. He has set out to cut the karmas… (8)
Sara Bharat bhraman kiya hai, nahin banai apni thaur.
Nagar-nagar mein ghoom-ghoom kar, yash phailaya charon or.
Agam path par chale nirantar, nahin chalaya apna panth.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥9॥
He has wandered all over India, never making a place his own. Going from town to town he spread his fame in all four directions. He walked continually on the path of the Agam; he never started a sect of his own. He has set out to cut the karmas… (9)
Simha samaan maha balshali, hathi sam ho unnat aap.
Surya kiran sam tej-punj ho, bhavya jeevon ka harte paap.
Meru sam hai dhyan aapka, karam-bali ka kar rahe ant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥10॥
Mighty in strength like a lion, lofty like an elephant; a mass of brilliance like the rays of the sun, removing the sins of bhavya souls. Your meditation is like Mount Meru; you are making an end of the mighty karma. He has set out to cut the karmas… (10)
Pavan samaan vicharne wale, chandra kiran sam sheetal jaan.
Baal samaan bhadra parinami, sagar sam gambhir mahan.
"Prabhav" badhe din raat aapka, aap hamare ho Bhagwant.
Nikal pade hain karm kaatne… ॥11॥
Wandering like the wind, cool as the rays of the moon; innocent in disposition like a child, deep and great like the ocean. May your influence (prabhav) grow day and night; you are our Lord. He has set out to cut the karmas… (11)
Teen lok kagaj karoon, lekhani sab vanaray.
Sab sagar syahi karoon, Guru gun likha na jaay.
Were I to make the three worlds my paper, all the forests my pens, and all the oceans my ink — still the virtues of the Guru could not be written.
Om Hreem Shattrimshat-Gunamandita-Acharya Vatsalya Varidhi Shri Vardhamansagar Mahayativarebhyo jayamala poornargham nirvapamiti svaha.
Guruvar tere naam se, bigde bante kaam.
Prabhav hit badhta rahe, Shivpur mein ho dhaam.
O great Guru, by your name ruined works are set right. May the welfare of Prabhav keep increasing; may his abode be in the City of Liberation.
Ityashirvadah — divya pushpanjali. (Thus the benediction — the divine handful of flowers.)
*

t: Aarti of the First Acharya, 108 Charitra Chakravarti Shri Shantisagar Ji Maharaj
grp: Aarti of the First Acharya, 108 Charitra Chakravarti Shri Shantisagar Ji Maharaj

c.b:
Shantisagar Maharaj, aaj thari aarti utaroon.
Aarti utaroon thane pal pal niharoon. Chandra sam deekhe teri kaay — aaj thari aarti utaroon…
Shantisagar Maharaj, today I perform your aarti. I perform your aarti; every moment I gaze upon you. Your body shines like the moon — today I perform your aarti…
Satyavati mata ke pyare, Bhimgaud ke raj dulare.
Daya-dharma avatar. — Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
Beloved of mother Satyavati, darling of Bhimgauda; the very embodiment of compassion and Dharma. — Today I perform your aarti…
Munivrat ki diksha hai dhari, charitra rath par kari savari.
Syadvad dhwaja phahray. — Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
You took the diksha of the Muni's vows and rode upon the chariot of Conduct, flying the banner of Syadvada. — Today I perform your aarti…
Agam-path ke the tum rahi, muni charya aakar batlai.
Maha tapasvi Nath! — Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
You were a traveller on the path of the Agam; you came and taught the conduct of the Muni, O great ascetic Lord! — Today I perform your aarti…
Pavan samaan vicharne wale, roke se na rukne wale.
Charitra-chakri raay. — Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
Wandering like the wind, not to be stopped by any hindrance; King among the Charitra Chakravartis. — Today I perform your aarti…
Sarparaj tan par chadh aaya, Simharaj se bhay nahin khaya.
Parishaha sahe apaar. — Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
The king of serpents climbed upon your body; you felt no fear of the king of lions. You bore boundless hardships. — Today I perform your aarti…
Guruvar tumse kuchh na chahen, dharma marg par hamen lagaven.
Shir par rahe tera haath. — Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
O great Guru, we ask nothing of you but this: set us on the path of Dharma. May your hand remain on our head. — Today I perform your aarti…
Agam mandir aap bachaya, mithyatam ko door bhagaya.
Prabhav badhe din raat. — Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
You saved the Agam and the temples; you drove far away the darkness of mithyatva. May Prabhav's welfare grow day and night. — Today I perform your aarti…
Shantisagar Maharaj, aaj thari aarti utaroon…
Aarti utaroon thane pal-pal niharoon.
Chandra sam deekhe thari kaay… Aaj thari aarti utaroon…
Shantisagar Maharaj, today I perform your aarti… I perform your aarti; every moment I gaze upon you. Your body shines like the moon… Today I perform your aarti…
